Regulation: B.C. Reg. 136/2026
Made under: Workers Compensation Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 20, 2026

B.C. Reg. 136/2026, deposited July 20, 2026, under theWORKERS COMPENSATION ACT[sections 110, 111 and 117]. Resolution of the Workers’ Compensation Board, dated July 16, 2026. The Workers’ Compensation Board orders that, effective March 1, 2027, the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97, is amended as set out in the attached Appendix. — W. L. CRONK,Chair, Board of Directors. 1	Section 12.74 of the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97, is amended (a)	by adding the following subsection: (0.1)	For the purposes of this section and sections 12.75 to 12.80.2, a lifting device that is designed for the purpose of facilitating the parking or storage of vehicles is not an automotive lift., (b)	by repealing subsection (1) and substituting the following: (1)	An automotive lift must not be operated unless it meets the requirements of one of the following standards: (a)ANSI Standard ANSI/ALI ALCTV-2025, American National Standard for Automotive Lifts –    Safety Requirements for Construction, Testing, and Validation; (b)ANSI Standard ANSI/ALI ALCTV-2017, American National Standard for Automotive Lifts –    Safety Requirements for Construction, Testing, and Validation; (c)ANSI Standard ANSI/ALI ALCTV-2011, American National Standard for Automotive Lifts –    Safety Requirements for Construction, Testing, and Validation; (d)ANSI Standard ANSI/ALI ALCTV-2006, American National Standard for Automotive Lifts –    Safety Requirements for Construction, Testing and Validation; (e)ANSI Standard ANSI/ALI ALCTV-1998, American National Standard for Automotive Lifts –    Safety Requirements for Construction, Testing and Validation; (g)EN 1493:2010 Vehicle Lifts., (c)	by adding the following subsection: (1.1)	Despite subsection (1), an automotive lift that does not meet one of the standards under that subsection may be operated if the following conditions are met: (a)	at least once every 4 months, the automotive lift passes an inspection that is carried out by a qualified person and that includes an inspection of (i)	the inspection points specified in section 6.2.4 ofANSI Standard ANSI/ALI ALOIM-2020, American National Standard for Automotive Lifts –    Safety Requirements for Operation, Inspection and Maintenance, and (ii)	any other inspection points that have been identified by the manufacturer of the automotive lift as requiring inspection annually or more frequently than annually; (b)	at least once every 12 months, the automotive lift passes an inspection that is carried out by a person who is certified as a lift inspector by the Automotive Lift Institute, Inc.;

minutes_briefs.title: BC automotive lifts must meet new safety standards or pass inspections starting March 1, 2027
minutes_briefs.summary: BC has changed the rules for automotive lifts (the machines that raise vehicles for repair work) under the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation. Starting March 1, 2027, a lift can only be used if it meets one of the listed safety standards, such as ANSI/ALI ALCTV or EN 1493:2010. Lifts that don't meet a listed standard can still be used, but only if they pass an inspection by a qualified person at least every 4 months and a full inspection by an Automotive Lift Institute certified inspector at least once every 12 months. The change also clarifies that equipment designed for parking or storing vehicles is not an automotive lift.
minutes_briefs.action_required: Check whether your automotive lifts meet a listed standard, and if not, set up the required 4-month and 12-month inspection schedule before March 1, 2027.

key_dates.label: BC automotive lift safety standard requirements take effect
